title: Normal functions: fixed points, epsilon numbers, and Goodstein sequences
summary: Normal ordinal functions have arbitrarily large fixed points; epsilon zero bounds finite hereditary expressions and measures Goodstein descent.
abstract: Repeatedly raising omega to an ordinal power leads to a first ordinal that equals omega raised to itself, called epsilon zero. Every smaller ordinal has a finite expression made from powers of omega, with the exponents expanded in the same way. More generally, any strictly increasing ordinal function that preserves limits has points it leaves unchanged beyond every ordinal. The finite expressions below epsilon zero also explain a surprising fact about natural numbers: every Goodstein sequence, formed by repeatedly increasing the base in a number’s hereditary representation and subtracting one, eventually reaches zero even when its terms initially grow.

based_on.title: Set Theory
